title: OpenAI pays $3.2m to settle a US claim it favoured visa workers over Americans
excerpt: OpenAI will pay $3.2m to settle a US Justice Department claim that it favoured temporary-visa workers over Americans in a green-card hiring process.
content_html:
OpenAI has agreed to pay $3.2m to settle a US government claim. The allegation: it favoured workers on temporary visas over American workers. The Justice Department announced the deal on Tuesday. It resolves claims that the company broke federal anti-discrimination law when recruiting for a set of roles.

The department’s Civil Rights Division said OpenAI OpCo LLC and its subsidiary Statsig had violated the Immigration and Nationality Act. The alleged discrimination happened during the Permanent Labor Certification process, known as PERM. That is the step where an employer sponsors a worker for a green card. First, it must show it could not find a qualified American for the job.

The Justice Department laid out what it said it found. OpenAI did not post the PERM roles on its external careers site, it said. It advertised other jobs there as normal. It required paper applications by mail for those roles, while accepting electronic ones elsewhere. And it advertised some positions on late-night radio. Fewer than ten jobs were at issue.

What OpenAI agreed to

Of the $3.2m, OpenAI will pay $1.2m in civil penalties. It will put another $2m into a fund to compensate the affected workers. The company also agreed to change how it recruits. It will post PERM roles on its public careers site and accept electronic applications. It will also retrain staff, revise its policies, and submit to Justice Department monitoring.

Harmeet Dhillon, who heads the Civil Rights Division, said preferring visa holders over US workers for jobs is illegal. The settlement, she added, makes OpenAI “redress harm and change its recruitment practices.” It gives American workers a fair shot at the roles. A spokesperson for OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment.

The PERM programme lets employers sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency when they cannot find a qualified American. During that process, it bars them from discriminating on the basis of citizenship. The Justice Department said this was its thirteenth such settlement since it relaunched its Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative in 2025.

The settlement adds to a busy legal stretch for OpenAI. The company is separately fighting a trade-secrets suit from Apple. The Justice Department has pressed similar cases against other large companies too. And employers across the industry are weighing how they hire for sought-after technology jobs. OpenAI’s own presence in Washington has grown alongside its business.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 已同意支付 320 万美元来解决美国政府的索赔。 指控：它比美国工人更有利于持有临时签证的工人。 司法部周二宣布了这项交易。 它解决了有关该公司在招聘一系列职位时违反联邦反歧视法的指控。

该部门的民权部门表示 OpenAI OpCo LLC 及其子公司 Statsig 违反了《移民和国籍法》。 所谓的歧视发生在永久劳工认证（PERM）过程中。 这是雇主赞助工人获得绿卡的步骤。 首先，它必须表明它无法找到合格的美国人来完成这项工作。

司法部公布了其所称的发现内容。 OpenAI 表示，并未在其外部招聘网站上发布 PERM 职位。 它照常在那里发布其他职位的广告。 这些职位要求通过邮寄方式提交纸质申请，同时在其他地方接受电子申请。 它还在深夜广播中刊登了一些职位的广告。 受影响的工作岗位不到十个。

OpenAI 同意的内容

在 320 万美元中，OpenAI 将支付 120 万美元的民事罚款。 该公司将另外投入 200 万美元设立基金，以补偿受影响的工人。 该公司还同意改变招聘方式。 它将在其公共职业网站上发布 PERM 职位并接受电子申请。 它还将重新培训员工、修改政策并接受司法部的监督。

民权部门负责人哈米特·迪隆 (Harmeet Dhillon) 表示，优先考虑签证持有者而不是美国工人是非法的。 她补充说，此次和解将使 OpenAI “纠正伤害并改变其招聘做法。” 它让美国工人有公平的机会担任这些角色。 OpenAI 的发言人没有回应置评请求。

PERM 计划允许雇主在找不到合格的美国人时担保外国工人获得永久居留权。 在此过程中，它禁止他们基于公民身份进行歧视。 司法部表示，这是自 2025 年重新启动“保护美国工人倡议”以来第 13 个此类和解协议。

此次和解让 OpenAI 的法律事务更加繁忙。 该公司正在单独应对苹果公司提起的商业秘密诉讼。 司法部也对其他大公司提出了类似的诉讼。 整个行业的雇主都在权衡如何招聘热门的技术职位。 OpenAI 在华盛顿的业务随着其业务的发展而不断发展。
